biography: Francisco Costa hails from the vibrant streets of São Paulo, Brazil, a city that breathes motorsport. Unlike many of his peers who grew up karting, Francisco's entry into racing was unconventional. He spent his early teens honing his reflexes and racecraft on sim racing platforms, dominating online leagues under the moniker 'Calculista'. A local businessman, impressed by Francisco's virtual prowess, sponsored him in a regional Formula Vee series. His transition to real-world racing was seamless. Francisco’s meticulous approach quickly made him a force to be reckoned with. He spent two years meticulously gathering data in Formula 3 before making the jump to Formula 2. Now at 24, he's reached what many consider his peak, meticulously working his way up the ladder and demonstrating a level of calculated aggression that sets him apart. He's a driver who's not afraid to play the long game, understanding that consistency and strategy are just as important as outright speed.
drivingStyle: Francisco's driving style is the epitome of calculated precision. He doesn't often engage in risky maneuvers, preferring to maintain consistent lap times and exploit the mistakes of others. His corner entry is smooth and controlled, sacrificing initial speed for a more stable exit. Tire management is his forte; he can seemingly coax extra laps out of a set of tires when others are struggling with grip. He thrives under pressure, remaining calm and composed even in the most intense situations, a trait that earned him the nickname 'Ice Man' early in his career.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos. Rossi, known for his flamboyant style, clashes with Francisco's reserved demeanor and calculated approach. Their racing styles also differ, with Rossi favoring aggressive overtakes and Francisco preferring strategic positioning.

A strategic battle. Dubois and Costa are both masters of tire management and strategy, leading to intense battles where every tenth of a second and pit stop decision matters. The mutual respect is high, but the competition is fierce.
A difference in background. Tanaka, a well-funded driver backed by a major corporation, initially dismissed Francisco's sim racing background. Francisco used his skills to quickly surpass Tanaka.

quirks: Always wears the same faded lucky t-shirt under his race suit.
Spends exactly 15 minutes in complete silence before each race, visualizing every corner.
Refuses to sign autographs until he's analyzed his race data.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about who's the fastest for one lap, it's about who's the smartest for every lap.
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula 2 championship after a season-long battle, securing the title in the final race with a perfectly executed strategy and flawless tire management.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in his debut Formula 2 race due to a rare lapse in concentration, costing him valuable points and denting his confidence early in the season.
